_meta.description: Curated, plain-language drug facts used as the trusted knowledge base for RAG. Summarised from public prescribing information (openFDA drug labels / DailyMed SPL) and Indian package inserts. Doses are deliberately excluded.
_meta.review_note: Facts are general and conservative. Before production use, have a pharmacist review every entry, or replace with sections ingested by scripts/ingest_openfda.py.

drugs.drug_class: Pain reliever and fever reducer (analgesic, antipyretic)
uses: Reduces fever
Relieves mild to moderate pain such as headache, toothache, body ache, back pain and period pain
Relieves aches from cold and flu
drugs.how_it_works: It lowers the brain's pain and temperature signals. It does not reduce swelling much.
serious_side_effects: Liver damage, especially if more than the label allows is taken, or taken with alcohol
Serious skin reactions (red, peeling or blistering skin): stop and get help
Allergic reaction: swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing
who_should_not_take: People with severe liver disease
People allergic to paracetamol
Anyone already taking another medicine that contains paracetamol (many cold and flu products do)
warnings: Taking too much can cause severe liver damage that may not show symptoms at first
Avoid alcohol
Check other medicines for hidden paracetamol
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, away from light and out of reach of children.

similar_medicines.name: Ibuprofen
similar_medicines.note: Different medicine (an NSAID) for pain and fever that also reduces swelling. Not the same salt.

drugs.rx_status: Over the counter (higher strengths need a prescription)
uses: Relieves pain such as headache, toothache, muscle ache and period pain
Reduces fever
Reduces swelling and pain in arthritis
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks body chemicals (prostaglandins) that cause pain, fever and swelling.
serious_side_effects: Stomach bleeding or ulcers: black or bloody stools, vomiting blood
Higher risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with long use
Kidney problems
Allergic reaction: wheezing, swelling, hives
who_should_not_take: People with a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding
People who had asthma or allergy after aspirin or other NSAIDs
People with serious heart, kidney or liver disease
Late pregnancy (last 3 months) unless a doctor says so
Right before or after heart bypass surgery
warnings: Risk of stomach bleeding is higher in people over 60, with alcohol, or with blood thinners or steroids
Do not combine with other NSAIDs
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, out of reach of children.

similar_medicines.name: Naproxen
similar_medicines.note: Another NSAID with similar uses and risks.

similar_medicines.name: Paracetamol
similar_medicines.note: For pain and fever without the stomach risks of NSAIDs, but no anti-swelling effect.

drugs.rx_status: Over the counter, but low-strength daily use should be advised by a doctor
uses: Low-strength aspirin is used, on a doctor's advice, to lower the chance of heart attack or stroke in people at risk
drugs.how_it_works: It makes platelets less sticky so blood clots form less easily.
serious_side_effects: Stomach or gut bleeding: black stools, vomiting blood
Bleeding that will not stop
Allergic reaction or asthma attack
Ringing in the ears
who_should_not_take: Children and teenagers, especially with viral illness (risk of Reye's syndrome)
People with bleeding disorders or active stomach ulcers
People allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs
Late pregnancy unless a doctor says so
warnings: Do not start or stop daily aspirin without asking a doctor
Tell your dentist or surgeon you take it
drugs.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. A strong vinegar smell means the tablets have broken down.

uses: Relieves sneezing, runny nose and itchy, watery eyes from allergies (hay fever)
Relieves itching and rash from hives
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks histamine, a chemical the body releases during an allergic reaction.
serious_side_effects: Allergic reaction to the medicine itself: swelling, trouble breathing
Trouble passing urine
who_should_not_take: People allergic to cetirizine or hydroxyzine
People with severe kidney disease unless a doctor advises
warnings: May cause drowsiness: be careful when driving
Alcohol and sleep medicines can add to drowsiness
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Fexofenadine
similar_medicines.note: Another antihistamine, less likely to cause sleepiness.

uses: Relieves sneezing, runny nose and itchy eyes from allergies
Relieves itching from hives
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks histamine, which causes allergy symptoms.
serious_side_effects: Allergic reaction: swelling, rash, trouble breathing
Fast or uneven heartbeat (rare)
who_should_not_take: People allergic to loratadine or desloratadine
People with liver or kidney disease should ask a doctor first
warnings: Less likely than older antihistamines to cause sleepiness, but it can
drugs.storage: Store at room temperature in a dry place.

drugs.rx_status: Over the counter in many countries
uses: Relieves allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose and itchy eyes
Relieves itching from hives
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks histamine, and is less likely to reach the brain and cause sleepiness.
serious_side_effects: Allergic reaction: swelling, rash, trouble breathing
who_should_not_take: People allergic to fexofenadine
People with kidney disease should ask a doctor first
warnings: Fruit juices (grapefruit, orange, apple) can reduce how well it works
Antacids with aluminium or magnesium can reduce absorption
drugs.storage: Store at room temperature in a dry place.

uses: Controls blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, together with diet and exercise
drugs.how_it_works: It reduces sugar made by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.
common_side_effects: Low vitamin B12 with long-term use
serious_side_effects: Lactic acidosis (rare but serious): unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, feeling very weak or cold. Get emergency help.
who_should_not_take: People with severe kidney disease
People with metabolic acidosis or diabetic ketoacidosis
People who drink heavily
warnings: May need to be stopped before scans that use iodine contrast dye or before surgery, as a doctor advises
Do not start or stop without a doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Glimepiride
similar_medicines.note: A different diabetes medicine (sulfonylurea); not a replacement without a doctor.

uses: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, together with diet and exercise
drugs.how_it_works: It helps the pancreas release more insulin.
common_side_effects: Low blood sugar: shakiness, sweating, hunger, confusion
serious_side_effects: Severe low blood sugar: fainting, seizures. Get emergency help.
Serious skin or allergic reactions
who_should_not_take: People with type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis
People allergic to sulfonylureas or sulfa drugs should tell their doctor
warnings: Skipping meals or drinking alcohol raises the risk of low blood sugar
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Metformin
similar_medicines.note: A different type of diabetes medicine.

uses: Treats high blood pressure
Prevents chest pain (angina)
drugs.how_it_works: It relaxes blood vessels so blood flows more easily.
serious_side_effects: Worsening chest pain or heart attack symptoms, especially when starting
Very low blood pressure: fainting
who_should_not_take: People allergic to amlodipine
People with very low blood pressure or severe narrowing of the aortic valve should tell their doctor
warnings: Do not stop suddenly without a doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

similar_medicines.name: Losartan
similar_medicines.note: A different type of blood pressure medicine.

drugs.drug_class: Blood pressure medicine (angiotensin receptor blocker, ARB)
uses: Treats high blood pressure
Protects the kidneys in some people with type 2 diabetes
Lowers stroke risk in some people with an enlarged heart
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks a hormone that narrows blood vessels.
serious_side_effects: Swelling of face, lips or throat
High potassium: weakness, uneven heartbeat
Kidney problems
Fainting from low blood pressure
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women: it can harm the unborn baby
People with diabetes who take aliskiren
warnings: Tell a doctor right away if you become pregnant
Ask before using potassium supplements or salt substitutes
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Amlodipine
similar_medicines.note: A different type of blood pressure medicine.

drugs.drug_class: Blood pressure medicine (angiotensin receptor blocker, ARB)
uses: Treats high blood pressure
Lowers the risk of heart attack and stroke in some high-risk people
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks a hormone that narrows blood vessels.
serious_side_effects: Swelling of face, lips or throat
High potassium
Kidney problems
Fainting from low blood pressure
who_should_not_take: Pregnant women: it can harm the unborn baby
People with diabetes who take aliskiren
People with severe liver problems
warnings: Tell a doctor right away if you become pregnant
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C. Keep in the original strip until use; tablets absorb moisture.

uses: Lowers 'bad' (LDL) cholesterol and triglycerides
Lowers the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at risk
drugs.how_it_works: It reduces how much cholesterol the liver makes.
serious_side_effects: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine (muscle breakdown)
Liver problems: yellow skin or eyes, dark urine
Higher blood sugar
who_should_not_take: Pregnant or breastfeeding women
People with active liver disease
warnings: Large amounts of grapefruit juice can raise its level in the blood
Many medicines interact with it: tell your doctor what else you take
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

drugs.rx_status: Over the counter for frequent heartburn; prescription for other uses
uses: Treats acid reflux and heartburn (GERD)
Helps heal stomach and duodenal ulcers
Used with antibiotics to clear H. pylori infection
drugs.how_it_works: It lowers the amount of acid the stomach makes.
serious_side_effects: Severe diarrhoea that does not stop (C. difficile infection)
Kidney inflammation: less urine, blood in urine
Low magnesium with long use: muscle cramps, uneven heartbeat
Higher risk of bone fractures with long use
who_should_not_take: People allergic to PPIs
People taking rilpivirine (an HIV medicine)
warnings: Heartburn with chest pain, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools needs a doctor right away
Long-term use should be reviewed by a doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Keep capsules in the strip.

similar_medicines.name: Famotidine
similar_medicines.note: A different type of acid reducer (H2 blocker).

sources: openFDA drug label: omeprazole delayed-release capsules

uses: Treats acid reflux and heartburn (GERD)
Helps heal damage to the food pipe caused by acid
Treats conditions where the stomach makes too much acid
drugs.how_it_works: It lowers the amount of acid the stomach makes.
serious_side_effects: Severe diarrhoea that does not stop
Kidney inflammation
Low magnesium with long use
Higher risk of bone fractures with long use
who_should_not_take: People allergic to PPIs
People taking rilpivirine
warnings: Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Long-term use should be reviewed by a doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.
sources: openFDA drug label: pantoprazole sodium delayed-release tablets

drugs.rx_status: Over the counter (low strength); prescription (higher strength)
uses: Relieves and prevents heartburn and acid indigestion
Treats stomach ulcers and acid reflux
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks histamine signals that tell the stomach to make acid.
serious_side_effects: Confusion or agitation, more likely in older people or those with kidney disease
Uneven heartbeat (rare)
who_should_not_take: People allergic to famotidine or other H2 blockers
warnings: People with kidney disease should ask a doctor first
See a doctor for heartburn lasting more than 2 weeks
drugs.storage: Store at room temperature in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Omeprazole
similar_medicines.note: A stronger type of acid reducer (PPI).

uses: Treats bacterial infections such as ear, nose, throat, chest, skin and urinary infections
Used with other medicines to clear H. pylori stomach infection
drugs.how_it_works: It kills bacteria by damaging their cell walls. It does not work for colds or flu (viruses).
serious_side_effects: Severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling, trouble breathing. Get emergency help.
Severe or bloody diarrhoea
Serious skin reactions
who_should_not_take: People allergic to penicillin or similar antibiotics (cephalosporins: tell your doctor)
warnings: Never use leftover antibiotics: the wrong antibiotic or an incomplete course can cause resistance
People with mononucleosis (glandular fever) are more likely to get a rash
drugs.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

similar_medicines.name: Amoxicillin + clavulanic acid
similar_medicines.note: Combination with a wider range; prescription only.

uses: Treats bacterial infections of the chest, throat, sinuses, ears and skin
Treats some sexually transmitted infections
drugs.how_it_works: It stops bacteria from making proteins they need to grow. It does not work for viral infections.
serious_side_effects: Uneven or fast heartbeat (QT prolongation): fainting, palpitations
Severe allergic or skin reaction
Liver problems: yellow skin, dark urine
Severe or bloody diarrhoea
who_should_not_take: People allergic to azithromycin, erythromycin or similar antibiotics
People who had liver problems from azithromycin before
warnings: Never use leftover antibiotics
People with heart rhythm problems should tell their doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place.

uses: Replaces thyroid hormone when the thyroid is underactive (hypothyroidism)
drugs.how_it_works: It is a man-made copy of the hormone the thyroid gland normally makes.
common_side_effects: Usually few side effects at the right strength
Signs of too much hormone: fast heartbeat, sweating, shakiness, weight loss, trouble sleeping
serious_side_effects: Chest pain or fast, uneven heartbeat
It must not be used for weight loss: large amounts can be dangerous
who_should_not_take: People with untreated adrenal gland problems
People with an overactive thyroid
warnings: Many foods and medicines (calcium, iron, antacids) affect absorption: ask a pharmacist about timing
Strength is very individual; do not use someone else's tablets
drugs.storage: Store below 25°C, protected from light and moisture. Keep in the original pack.

similar_medicines.name: Liothyronine
similar_medicines.note: A different thyroid hormone; prescription only.

sources: openFDA drug label: levothyroxine sodium tablets

uses: Helps prevent asthma attacks (not for a sudden attack)
Prevents exercise-induced breathing problems
Relieves allergy symptoms when other medicines are not suitable
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that cause swelling and tightening in the airways.
serious_side_effects: Mood and behaviour changes: agitation, bad dreams, depression, suicidal thoughts. Contact a doctor right away.
Allergic reaction
who_should_not_take: People allergic to montelukast
warnings: It does not treat a sudden asthma attack; keep your rescue inhaler
Watch for mood changes, especially in children
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light and moisture.

similar_medicines.name: Montelukast + levocetirizine
similar_medicines.note: Combination tablet common in India; prescription only.

uses: Relieves pain and swelling in arthritis
Relieves pain such as back pain, sprains and period pain
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks body chemicals that cause pain and swelling.
serious_side_effects: Stomach bleeding or ulcers: black stools, vomiting blood
Higher risk of heart attack and stroke
Liver problems
Kidney problems
who_should_not_take: People with stomach ulcers or bleeding
People who had asthma or allergy after aspirin or other NSAIDs
People with serious heart, liver or kidney disease
Late pregnancy unless a doctor says so
warnings: Do not combine with other NSAIDs
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C, protected from moisture.

similar_medicines.name: Aceclofenac
similar_medicines.note: Closely related NSAID common in India.

sources: openFDA drug label: diclofenac sodium delayed-release tablets

uses: Prevents nausea and vomiting from chemotherapy, radiation or surgery
drugs.how_it_works: It blocks serotonin, a chemical that can trigger vomiting.
serious_side_effects: Uneven heartbeat (QT prolongation)
Serotonin syndrome when used with some other medicines: agitation, fever, fast heartbeat
Allergic reaction
who_should_not_take: People taking apomorphine
People allergic to ondansetron or similar medicines
warnings: People with heart rhythm problems or low potassium or magnesium should tell their doctor
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C, protected from light.

similar_medicines.name: Domperidone
similar_medicines.note: A different anti-nausea medicine (not sold in the US).

drugs.drug_class: Heart and blood pressure medicine (beta blocker)
uses: Treats high blood pressure
Prevents chest pain (angina)
Used after a heart attack and in some heart failure
drugs.how_it_works: It slows the heart and lowers the force of each beat.
serious_side_effects: Very slow heartbeat or fainting
Shortness of breath or wheezing
Worsening heart failure: swelling, weight gain
who_should_not_take: People with very slow heartbeat or certain heart blocks
People with severe circulation problems
People with untreated phaeochromocytoma
warnings: Stopping suddenly can cause chest pain or heart attack: only stop with a doctor's plan
May hide signs of low blood sugar
drugs.storage: Store below 30°C, protected from moisture.
